findings.title: Looking at the scene arrives late and all at once
findings.setting: pick_target, 4000 demonstrations, one policy evaluated as it trains (averaged weights), 100 unseen layouts

note.text: The patch-token policy with instruction tokens and no history, 48.9M parameters. It stays at 2% or less for the first 1.5M samples, then covers most of the way within the next million; the final checkpoint scored 83/100 on a second set of layouts. With 1500 demonstrations and 1.0M samples the same policy ends at 5%, so a budget that ends too early reads as a design that does not work.

statements.about: The findings the landing page states in a sentence or two each, below the hero. Each names the chapter that explains it (its file name without .md) and the notebook heading its numbers are under (the results page anchors its sections by that heading). Every number in a text is in its quotes, word for word.

items.title: Looking at the scene arrives late, and all at once
items.text: The same policy, on the same 4000 demonstrations, succeeded 1% of the time after 1.0M training samples, 36% after 2.0M and 85% after 5.0M (averaged weights). Nothing in its training loss announces the change, so a budget that ends too early reads as a design that does not work.

items.title: The previous action as an input lets a policy stop looking
items.text: Given its previous action as an input, the policy read the target from that input instead of from the cameras. As served it succeeded in 1/100 episodes; told the expert’s first command as its previous action, in 22/100; with the expert driving the first 10 steps, in 77/100. In training that slot held the expert’s first command, which already points at the target.
items.section: What the history policy depends on
quotes: ### What the history policy depends on

| the previous action sent with the first query is the expert's first command | 22/100 |
| the expert drives the first 10 steps, then the policy takes over | 77/100 |
the expert's first command, which already points at the target, is an input in training

items.title: A policy that succeeds may look only once
items.text: Sent only the first camera frame for the whole episode, the policy that succeeds in 85/100 still closed nearest the named object in 99% of episodes, though only 1/100 succeeded. When the object is moved 80 mm at step 20 of the reach, it closes a median 8 mm from where the object was and 78 mm from where it is: 0/96.
items.section: What the no-history policy depends on
quotes: ### What the no-history policy depends on
| the first frame's images are sent for the whole episode | 1/100 | 99% | 17 mm |
The named object is moved once per episode, 80 mm in a random direction unless stated

items.title: What the demonstrations contain decides what the policy looks at
items.text: Same policy, same 4000 episodes, different content. Trained on one clean pass per layout from a single start pose, it succeeded in 93/100, and in 9/100 when each episode began from a random pose. Trained on demonstrations from random start poses, it succeeded in 98/100, and in 97/100 from random poses.

items.title: Self-correction has to be in the data
items.text: Trained on demonstrations in which the object is moved and the expert recovers, the policy follows a moved object (79/96 when it is moved at step 20 of the reach) and tries again after a missed grasp: with the object moved as the gripper closes, it succeeded in 78/99 and made a second attempt in all 99.
items.section: How each policy copes outside the conditions it was trained in
quotes: in 1505 episodes the object is moved once (during the reach or as the gripper closes) and the expert plans again

items.title: A position table in half precision merged most positions
items.text: The rotary position table was computed in bfloat16, which keeps 8 significant bits: 641 distinct positions out of 2048, and the policy’s 15 action tokens shared 8 of them. Computed in float32, the same recipe ends at 93% instead of 83% (trained weights), and at 96% instead of 90% with a second pair of seeds, and starts to look earlier: after 1.0M samples it closed at the named object in 65% of episodes instead of 35%.
